name: Cefaclor
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero
summary: Cefaclor is 60% to 85% excreted unchanged in urine, but its half-life rises only from about 0.6–0.9 hours to 2.3–2.8 hours even with no kidney function. The US label says it may be given in kidney impairment with the dose usually unchanged. Hemodialysis shortens the half-life by 25% to 30%.
kidney_function_basis: Label gives no kidney measure or bands.

bands.recommendation: Dose usually unchanged (label). Watch for toxicity, as cefaclor is substantially excreted by the kidney (label geriatric use).

dialyzable: Partly: hemodialysis shortens the half-life by 25% to 30% (label); not shown to help in overdose.
monitoring: Kidney function in older adults (label); diarrhea (CDAD); serum-sickness-like reactions in children.

pediatric.usual_dose: 20 mg/kg/day divided every 8 hours; serious infections and otitis media 40 mg/kg/day; otitis media and pharyngitis may be divided every 12 hours (label).
